title: Medication errors after product substitution during drug shortages: a retrospective review of incident reports and pharmacist interventions
subtitle: Three shortage episodes, 2024 to 2025, Ellery Park Hospital
statement: Three drug shortages between March 2024 and October 2025 forced product substitutions with different concentrations or vial sizes. Staff reported near misses, but shortage-related incidents are not flagged and nobody knows how often substitutions were followed by errors, of what kind, where in the medication process, or whether some substitutions were riskier than others.
whoAffected: Inpatients, including children, receiving the substituted products; nurses, prescribers and pharmacists who handle substitutions; the medication safety program.
whatHurts: Concentration and dilution changes can lead to wrong doses or rates, including with high-alert medicines such as intravenous potassium.
currentPractice: Alerts and electronic prescribing changes at each substitution; no review of what happened afterwards.
whyNow: Shortages recur and the next substitution plan should be informed by what went wrong in the last three.
constraints: Existing incident reports and the pharmacy intervention log only; chart review limited to 150 cases. One pharmacy resident for 100 hours between November 2026 and April 2027. Results reported by shortage episode, never naming staff or wards.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients receive the right dose at the right rate when a product has to be substituted.
summary: Problem framed as a retrospective review of substitution-related errors in three shortage episodes.
